claim: Sacro Monte di Orta is a UNESCO World Heritage site with 20 chapels on Saint Francis's life; chapels open 9:30-18:00 weekdays and 9:30-18:30 weekends/holidays from 29 March to 24 October 2026; free admission; about a 20-minute walk from Orta on a sloped paved cobbled road with steps.
quote: Monday to Friday from 9:30am. to 6:00pm; Saturday, Sunday and public holidays from 9:30am to 6:30pm

claim: The public Navigazione Orta boat service from Orta to Isola San Giulio runs every 15 minutes starting 9:00 a.m. daily, with a €5.00 return fare.
quote: €5,00* return ... Every 15 minutes ... starting at 9.00 a.m.

claim: Private motoscafi consortium boats cost about €5 round-trip and start earlier and run more frequently than the public ferry (€3.80 round-trip, every 30-45 minutes); crossing takes about 5 minutes.
quote: Motorboats cost €5 round-trip and start earlier and run more frequently ... Public ferries cost €3.80 round-trip ... every 30 to 45 minutes

claim: The Basilica di San Giulio dates to the 4th century (current 12th-century Romanesque structure built on a 5th-century church), with frescoes of the Apostles from the 14th-16th centuries and a four-pillared black marble pulpit with animal carvings as old as the church; San Giulio's remains lie in the crypt.
quote: The current 12th-century Romanesque structure was built on top of an older church from the 5th century ... frescoes depicting the Apostles ... between the 14th and 16th centuries

claim: Palazzotto della Comunità on Piazza Motta was built in 1582 and served as the meeting place for the General Council of the Republic of the Riviera d'Orta from 1345-1753; the Basilica frescoes include baroque works by Carlo Borsetti and Francesco del Cairo; Sacro Monte is about 24 minutes' walk from the main square.
quote: 1582 palace sits on Piazza Motta's left side and formerly served as the meeting place for the small Republic of the Riviera d'Orta's general council (1345-1753)

claim: Villa Crespi is the trailhead for walking routes that pass through Piazza Motta and connect to the surrounding lake panoramic trails.
quote: starts from Orta San Giulio, in particular from Piazza Motta ... At Villa Crespi you'll come to Crociera

claim: Sacro Monte di Orta sits on a hilltop overlooking the lake and Isola San Giulio; visitors should allow 1.5-2 hours and wear comfortable shoes.
quote: Admission is free, and you should allow 1.5-2 hours for your visit; comfortable shoes are highly recommended

claim: The Mater Ecclesiae Benedictine abbey on Isola San Giulio was founded in 1973 as a cloistered community of nuns dedicated to the Marian feast of Mary, Mater Ecclesiae; the nuns produce liturgical paraments.
quote: It was founded in 1973. It is dedicated to the Marian Patronal Feast of Mary, Mater Ecclesiae. The nuns are known for the production of paraments.

claim: Villa Crespi is roughly a 10-12 minute walk from Piazza Motta in Orta San Giulio; the historic centre is entirely pedestrianised with the Wednesday market on Piazza Motta dating to 1228.
quote: the quaint town of Orta San Giulio can be easily reached on foot from Villa Crespi with a beautiful 10-minute walk ... Since 1228, the market has been held here on Wednesdays

claim: Sacro Monte di Orta is roughly 600 metres from Villa Crespi and can be reached from the end of the Sacro Monte route down the other side of the hill to Villa Crespi in about 15 minutes.
quote: Just 600 meters from Villa Crespi ... from the end of the Sacro Monte course, you can descend on the other side of the hill and get to Villa Crespi in about 15 minutes

claim: The Way of Silence (Via del Silenzio) is a cobblestoned alleyway encircling the island lined with multilingual signs in four languages inviting silent reflection, taking around 10-30 minutes depending on pace.
quote: cobble-stoned alleyway that circles the island ... signs written in 4 languages with sayings to encourage reflection
